title: Utsunomiya — 宇都宮
goal: Introduce four sibling relationships with appropriate own-family/polite terms.

blocks.text: **Prefecture-name breakdown:** 栃: radical 木, きへん; right side 厉-shaped, with 厂 above 万. とち is the Japanese horse-chestnut tree word. Its detailed origin is uncertain in the consulted dictionary, so these are modern recognition pieces, not a claimed etymology. 木: its own tree radical, き; formal review. 栃木 is とちぎ, with ぎ in this learned name. 栃 remains assisted.
Utsunomiya is known for gyoza. Our fictional traveller meets siblings here. Food provides the setting; the language goal extends the parents/children vocabulary taught in Aizuwakamatsu.
**宇都宮で兄に会います。** うつのみやで あにに あいます。 — I meet my older brother in Utsunomiya.
The relation belongs to the speaker in this sentence. “Older/younger” compares siblings' ages; it does not mean old versus new like 古い/新しい. We do not infer who somebody is from a photograph alone.

items: **Character:** 宇 · **Meaning/reading here:** roof/space; う · **Radical/components:** 宀, うかんむり; 于 historically supplies sound · **Status:** Encounter.
**Character:** 都 · **Meaning/reading here:** capital/city; つ · **Radical/components:** 邑 as right 阝, おおざと; 者 sound component · **Status:** Encounter; right 阝 differs from left 阝/阜.
**Character:** 宮 · **Meaning/reading here:** shrine/palace; みや · **Radical/components:** 宀 above 呂-shaped section, historically a shortened sound component · **Status:** Encounter review from 宮城.

blocks.text: **宇都宮 / うつのみや** includes の in the name reading without a separate written の. Learn the full name; the component glosses do not prove how the city was named.

cards.title: 兄 and 姉: older siblings

blocks.text: **兄 / あに — my older brother; 姉 / あね — my older sister.** 兄 has radical 儿, にんにょう, below 口. 姉 has radical 女, おんなへん, beside 市-shaped strokes. “Woman plus city” is a recognition description, not an invented explanation of sisterhood.
**兄は学生です。** あには がくせいです。 — My older brother is a student.
**姉は先生です。** あねは せんせいです。 — My older sister is a teacher.
These occupations are fictional, not gender roles. 兄/姉 are the standard own-family terms when speaking to someone outside the family.

cards.title: 弟 and 妹: younger siblings

blocks.text: **弟 / おとうと — my younger brother; 妹 / いもうと — my younger sister.** 弟 has radical 弓, ゆみ, within its modern layered strokes; 妹 has 女 beside 未, a historical sound component. 未 differs from 末 in the relative lengths of the two upper horizontals.
**弟は日本に住んでいます。** おとうとは にほんに すんでいます。 — My younger brother lives in Japan.
**妹は本を読みます。** いもうとは ほんを よみます。 — My younger sister reads books.
おとうと and いもうと are complete word readings. Do not force a shared と segment into a rule for other family characters.

items: **Own-family description to an outsider:** 兄 / あに · **Polite/reference term for someone else's family:** お兄さん · **Reading:** おにいさん
**Own-family description to an outsider:** 姉 / あね · **Polite/reference term for someone else's family:** お姉さん · **Reading:** おねえさん
**Own-family description to an outsider:** 弟 / おとうと · **Polite/reference term for someone else's family:** 弟さん · **Reading:** おとうとさん
**Own-family description to an outsider:** 妹 / いもうと · **Polite/reference term for someone else's family:** 妹さん · **Reading:** いもうとさん

blocks.text: **お兄さんは学生ですか。** おにいさんは がくせいですか。 — Is your older brother a student?
**はい、兄は学生です。** はい、あには がくせいです。 — Yes, my older brother is a student.
Family members may address each other using お兄さん/お姉さん too. Context controls choice; the table is not a ban on those words inside one's own family.

cards.title: No confusion between parents and siblings

blocks.text: Review **父 / ちち**, my father; **母 / はは**, my mother; **子ども / こども**, child. **兄弟 / きょうだい — siblings/brothers**, useful whole compound, often used more broadly than literal brothers in ordinary contexts. **家族 / かぞく — family** is helped; 族 remains an encounter.
**家族は四人です。** かぞくは よにんです。 — My family has four people.
**兄弟は三人です。** きょうだいは さんにんです。 — There are three of us siblings.
The narrator is included in this stated siblings count. Do not assume every other “siblings” count always excludes or includes the speaker without context.
**だれ — who; 何人 / なんにん — how many people.** Pronunciation distinguishes the number question from 何 / なに in 何を読みますか.
**この人はだれですか。** このひとは だれですか。 — Who is this person?
**姉です。** あねです。 — It is my older sister.
**家族は何人ですか。** かぞくは なんにんですか。 — How many people are in your family?
**四人です。** よにんです。 — Four people.
Use introductions or stated relationships; appearance is insufficient to identify a sister rather than a friend.
**兄とご飯を食べます。** あにと ごはんを たべます。 — I eat a meal with my older brother.
**姉に会います。** あねに あいます。 — I meet my older sister.
**弟を待ちます。** おとうとを まちます。 — I wait for my younger brother.
**妹と話します。** いもうとと はなします。 — I talk with my younger sister.
The same family noun can take と, に or を according to its relationship with the verb. English “with/for” is not a reliable one-particle translation rule.
**来週の土曜日に兄と宇都宮に行きます。** らいしゅうの どようびに あにと うつのみやに いきます。 — Next Saturday I go to Utsunomiya with my older brother.
**午後一時に姉に会います。** ごごいちじに あねに あいます。 — I meet my older sister at 1 PM.
This fictional plan contains two kinds of に: calendar/clock time and the person met. Read each phrase by its role; multiple に in a sentence are not automatically an error.
**A: この人はだれですか。** このひとは だれですか。 — Who is this person?
**B: 妹です。** いもうとです。 — She is my younger sister.
**A: 妹さんは学生ですか。** いもうとさんは がくせいですか。 — Is your younger sister a student?
**B: はい、学生です。** はい、がくせいです。 — Yes, she is.
The listener switches to 妹さん when referring politely to the speaker's sister. The reply can omit the already understood topic; repeating 私の妹 in every line is unnecessary.

items: Read 宇都宮. **Answer:** うつのみや, including spoken の.
Read 兄, 姉, 弟, 妹. **Answers:** あに; あね; おとうと; いもうと.
What radical links 姉 and 妹? **Answer:** 女.
Politely ask about someone else's older sister. **Model:** お姉さんは学生ですか。
Read 四人 and 何人. **Answers:** よにん; なんにん.
Complete the waiting model: 弟＿＿待ちます。 **Answer:** を.

blocks.text: 宇都宮 is うつのみや. 兄/姉 are older siblings; 弟/妹 are younger siblings. Own-family terms and polite references differ: あに versus おにいさん, あね versus おねえさん. 姉/妹 share 女; 弟 is indexed under 弓. Read the speaker's relationship rather than guessing it from a picture.
**Recall:** “My younger sister is a student.” **Model:** 妹は学生です。 いもうとは がくせいです。 Next, Nikko adds everyday words for people and children.
